issue.body:
Previously, only static evaluation of `Array.slice` was implemented in
ngtsc's static evaluator. This commit adds support for `Array.concat`.

Closes #29835

body: @yantrab cold you share a repo with reproduction?

Yes,
```
git clone -b  update-angular  https://github.com/yantrab/nest-angular.git

 cd .\nest-angular\ && npm i

 cd .\client\ && ng serve
```

after very long time i get `ERROR in Expected array when reading property exports`



and in [this ](https://github.com/yantrab/yangular) repo i get:
```
ERROR in Unable to write a reference to TableComponent in C:/Users/yantr/Desktop/mat-virtual-table/projects/mat-virtual-table/src/lib/table.component.ts from C:/Users/yantr/Desktop/mat-virtual-table/projects/mat-virtual-table/src/lib/table.module.ts
i ｢wdm｣: Failed to compile.
i ｢wdm｣: Compiling...
```

@yantrab Thank you so much, that has been really helpful. The message `Expected array when reading property exports` is produced because at this moment, usage of tslib's `__spread` function usage as seen in `node_modules/mat-virtual-table/fesm5/mat-virtual-table.js#TableModule` is not recognized and prevents static analysis of the `NgModule.exports` value, which is required for the compiler to work. I created FW-1298 to track this.

I did not look into your second problem, could you perhaps open a new issue for that?

Thanks.
In fact, the second repo is 'mat-virtual-table'. that i knew it has a 'concat' in imports, and I tried to reduce the problem. I'll open a new one for this.

By the way, how can you get a more detailed log about the error?
And what about the time that it is takes, is that reasonable?

@yantrab I now spotted the `concat` in the imports, I am not sure however if that is causing the problem as 1.4.2 of `mat-virtual-table` has that `__spread` thing going on. I notice the `__spread` call has since been removed in 1.4.3. Are you still experiencing issues with that?

Regarding the performance: the initial time (with fresh `node_modules`) that you compile your Angular app with Ivy enabled is quite slow because ngcc (Angular Compatibility Compiler) will run AOT compilation for NPM libraries. This however is a one-time process per library installation, so subsequent runs should be quite a bit faster.

@JoostK we can confirm using spread syntax in module declaration triggers the error `ERROR in Expected array when reading property declarations` each time. 
```
exports: [
    ...gmdModules,
    ScrollDispatchModule,
  ],
```

It's quite useful to be able to use spread syntax when importing/exporting/declaring large number of modules/components.
@blackholegalaxy could you share the generated ES5 code of that module? If it uses `tslib.__spread(gmdModules)` it is not currently supported.

It seems to be compiled into `concat()` but I will look deeper to find a `__spread`. 

The fact is the error doesn't point where it failed its hard to debug. Will try more verbose build
@blackholegalaxy Could you share the code, even for the `concat()`?
